vehicles/rocket: "descends from long-range weapons built during the Second World War" - true of the lineage (V-2 to postwar missiles to launchers), but not literally of every modern launcher
vehicles/wagon: "was drawn into a circle for protection when travellers camped" - wagon trains did circle at camp, but historians say it was mainly to corral livestock; attack defence is partly folklore
vehicles/tractor: "is often painted green, red or blue by its maker" - rests on maker colour conventions (green, red, blue brands); true in general, not a physical property
vehicles/train: "makes a rhythmic clatter as its wheels cross joints in the track" - true on jointed track; modern continuously welded rail largely removes the clatter
vehicles/ferry: "is often run by a public transport authority" - many ferries are public, but many are privately operated; 'often' carries the claim
vehicles/van: "can be driven on an ordinary car licence in most places" - holds for light vans (up to about 3.5 t in Europe); larger vans need a higher category
vehicles/scooter: "became a style icon for young riders in postwar Italy" - true only of the motor scooter sense
"is limited to low speeds in cycle lanes in many cities" - e-scooter rules vary widely by city
vehicles/kayak: "was first built by Arctic peoples to hunt seals and fish" - the Arctic origin is standard; the exact prey mix varied by people and region
